title: Pragmata defies my expectations by selling 2.5 million copies in just 3 months as Capcom celebrates a very successful start to 2026
summary: It's good to see that at least someone's doing well.
body: Capcom just released its Q1 2026 financial report , and to absolutely no one's surprise, the company is doing well, really well. But to my surprise, so is Pragmata . As part of the report Capcom shared sales figures for its recent releases, and Pragmata sold more than 2.5 million copies since it was released earlier this year. Now, to be clear this isn't because I think Pragmata is a bad game—I liked its old-timey shooter vibes and QTE hacking when I played its preview way back when. And Justin Wagner really loved its puzzles, main duo, and "poignant" narrative moments in our Pragmata review . But even still it's a completely new story from Capcom with no existing fanbase to go to bat for it. (Image credit: Capcom) I also felt that its release fell a little flat as hype seemingly petered out rather quickly—I certainly didn't feel the need to tell the world about my adventures around the collapsing moonbase. Nevertheless, I'm happy that Pragmata was successful and that it translated into healthy sales numbers. Hopefully this gives Capcom renewed confidence when it comes to pursuing new worlds and ideas. Capcom also touts the Devil May Cry animated series and the latest Resident Evi…

title: You can now play Morrowind entirely in your browser: 'Honestly just wanted to see if it could be done'
summary: Good if you've got some downtime at work. On your lunch break, of course.
body: With Bethesda making us wait going on 15 long years for the next Elder Scrolls game (I'm not including Oblivion Remastered ), we've been left to our own devices. A phenomenon I've noticed spike as of late is calls for a Morrowind remaster, and a lot of chatter surrounding Bethesda's seminal 2002 RPG in general, like game devs weighing in on how it would fare if it came out today , and the history behind The Lusty Argonian Maid . We're all getting cabin fever. To make up for it not being ported to every platform in existence like its older sibling Skyrim, crafty Reddit user Dumpster Buddy (as spotted by Eurogamer ) has somehow managed to get Morrowind running in your browser . "I got OpenMW (the open-source Morrowind engine) compiling to WebAssembly," they explain, "so the whole game runs in a browser tab now. You open a link and you're standing in Seyda Neen. No install, no launcher." The most baffling detail is that it's the actual game engine flowing through your browser, "not a stream and not an emulator." It looks exactly like it would if you booted it up from Steam, you can save your progress, and it has controller and mod support. The developer is even considering adding fea…

body: Final Fantasy 14 has become just as much of a social chatroom as it has an MMO. You'd be hard-pressed to find a veteran Warrior of Light who hasn't spent copious amounts of time rummaging through their glamour dresser or paying regular visits to the aesthetician for a new hairstyle in order to perfectly present their ideal image as they idle in Limsa Lominsa or run around the expansion's latest player hub. That playstyle has led to an increasing demand for more flexibility and freedom in the way players can present their characters over the years which, for a long time, was met with a fair bit of resistance from director and producer Naoki Yoshida. Requests to unshackle gear from their job or role-based restrictions were long declined—once saying that "it would feel awkward if a Black Mage jumped into an instanced dungeon with full plate armour." (Image credit: Square Enix) That argument very much lost its juice as Final Fantasy 14 started adding in more gear that wasn't particularly befitting of any job or role—hell, the game literally added a full plate armour set for all classes before Yoshida ever made the above comment. title: I'm pretty sure we know Final Fantasy 14 Evercold's second job, unless Soken's playing a big trick on us
summary: Haven't you heard, about the bird?
body: Call me delusional, but I think I—well, a collection of sharp eyes from the Final Fantasy 14 community—have cracked what Final Fantasy 14: Evercold's next job is going to be. We were introduced to the Bastion during the latest fanfest, but we've still got one more job to go—a job we happen to know is a ranged physical dps. Pardon me while I gather my corkboard and red string—I'll be starting off with the strongest evidence to the weaker stuff, but I think you can make a compelling case that the job will be some sort of bird tamer with a crossbow. Firstly, because of lead composer and sound director Masayoshi Soken's tease at the fanfest, clipped here by Reddit user ParvatiLikeaRockstar . New ranged dps teased by Soken at Berlin fanfest from r/ffxiv In the first clip, we hear a magical charge-up, a click—like a crossbow string latching or being fired—and then an explosion. In the second, we very clearly hear a bird assailing an enemy, and more sounds akin to something being fired. In the recently-extended trailer itself, we see a miqo'te named Visna being harassed by her pet bird while checking a wand-like object for flaws. She flinches, touches the tip of the wand, and it explodes…

body: A few weeks ago Bethesda Studios hit the big red button and announced that both Fallout 3 and Fallout New Vegas remasters are in pre-production, but that wasn't all—there was also news of Fallout 76's next major expansion. "With nearly 70 free updates released to date, the journey is far from over. In fact, we have a major Fallout 76 expansion planned for next year; Raven Rock, a prequel story to Fallout 3." (Image credit: Bethesda) The last major expansion for Fallout 76 saw players venture to Ohio for the first time in Fallout lore in the Burning Springs expansion. Released around the Fallout TV show's season 2, Burning Springs was meant to marry the game with the show and its Fallout 3/ New Vegas inspirations ; aka, "desert, deathclaws, and raiders." But if Raven Rock is going to be a Fallout 3 prequel then, first off, it's going to be a very early one: 76 takes place over 100 years before Fallout 3. title: Consumer electronics companies were already worried about securing memory next year—now, supply is predicted to plummet by 70%
summary: No end in sight.
body: If you've been keeping up to date with news of the raging memory supply crisis , then I don't need to tell you how the AI industry's seemingly bottomless hunger for both system storage and RAM has significantly raised prices. Well, it turns out it can get worse than runaway costs, as manufacturers are even more concerned about securing supply, period . Apacer CEO C.K. Chang recently warned that memory shortages are expected to remain severe throughout 2026. He recently explained that securing supply is a bigger operational risk to Apacer now than paying high costs, as he expects memory manufacturers will release about 30% of their 2026 supply volume in 2027 (via DigiTimes ). Chang clarified that next year's limited supply won't be due to a fundamental shift in the market's structure. Still, in order to guard against such a shortfall, Apacer will attempt to secure as much inventory as it possibly can now. At the end of the 2026's first half, Apacer already held about $383 million worth of inventory. Many other consumer electronics companies are already thinking along similar lines, securing multi-year supply contracts and further ensuring the memory shortage won't ease in the near …

title: Nioh 3's first DLC hits in August, brings new weapons, a trip to the (sort of) future, and there's a mega-hard difficulty mode for the sickos
summary: Are you sickos?
body: I will be truthful: if you grabbed me by the lapels and demanded I tell you when Nioh 3 came out, I would answer something along the lines of 'the late 1980s'. The fact that the third Nioh—a rather good game, per our 90% Nioh 3 review —only released in February of this year feels like a weft in the tapestry of space-time. But so it was, and so it is that Nioh 3 will, on August 19, get its first DLC in the form of Hell Rising : "Our protagonist and appointed shogun, Takechiyo, journeys through time and is led to Edo in the future by an unknown yokai he met in his dreams," goes the blurb. "Edo in the future" is the year 1651, by the by. Things aren't looking great. "The large castle town that was once proof of the shogunate’s authority has transformed into a hellish wasteland plagued by the gales of the Crucible," rumbles the DLC description. I knew a guy in uni who called himself an alchemist from foreign lands, but he was just a Latvian guy who sold cannabis. The new DLC brings new gear with it. title: Alienware 34 AW3426DW review
summary: Alienware's updated 34-inch ultrawide OLED monitor is even more awesome than the original.
body: Can it really be well over four years since Alienware rolled out the AW3423DW , the first mainstream OLED gaming monitor? The AW3423DW wasn't perfect, but by many important gaming metrics, it absolutely monstered every LCD-based display. That model, of course, was a 34-inch ultrawide and now Alienware has released its most significant update yet for that form factor, the Alienware 34 AW3426DW . So, what does four years of OLED gaming monitor development buy you? In really simple terms, some new threads, a bit more brightness, and a higher refresh rate. But when you dig down into the details, there's way more going on here. Most importantly, Alienware has upgraded to Samsung's very latest QD-OLED panel tech, known as Penta Tandem. In terms of headline specs, that means a bump from 250 nits full-screen and 1,000 nits peak HDR brightness of that OG Alienware OLED, to 300 nits and 1,300 nits respectively. You also get an upgrade from VESA DisplayHDR 400 True Black to 500 True Black certification, again highlighting the punchier panel. title: You won't have to worry about limited bandwidth or data now that Valve has fixed  local network game transfers on Steam
summary: Sharing is caring—here's how to check your Steam client is up to date.
body: One saving grace of a flat mate is setting up 'family sharing' on each other's Steam libraries at the earliest opportunity. Another saving grace is leveraging local network game transfers to then have a go at whichever game has become your roommate's flavour of the month, and judging them accordingly. Recently though, Steam's local network game transfers hadn't been working as intended. For instance, some folk would attempt to kick off a local transfer, only for Steam to download via the internet instead. That's less than ideal if your bandwidth is scarce or you're working with limited data. Thankfully, Valve shipped a fix to the stable channel of the Steam Client on Monday. That means, you should now be able to transfer games between gaming desktops, laptops, and handhelds like the Steam Deck once more—so long as you've got the most up to date version of the Steam client installed. Stick with me, because I'll tell you how to check Steam is up to date on your PC and Steam Deck. To check you're up to date on PC, open the client, click 'Steam' in the top left corner, and click 'Check for Steam Client Updates…' from the drop down menu. title: 'Wtf is going on': Indie dev discovers their neglected Steam game is powering an Undertale multiplayer mod following its freak 1700% jump in player activity
summary: Little-known platformer Crashphalt is enjoying an unexpected popularity—but its players are enjoying something else.
body: A few months ago, indie developer RetroSpecter noticed something unusual about Crashphalt , their first completed game that launched on Steam in 2018: Since their last check-in on the neglected platformer, Crashphalt had suddenly gained over 500 reviews. In its first four years, it had barely managed a dozen. And almost none of those new reviewers had anything to say about Crashphalt itself. Mostly, they just talked about Undertale. (Image credit: Cold Pressed Games) "Does ANYONE want to play Undertale with me???" one reviewer writes. Another calls Crashphalt the "best game to never actually play." Others insist that "Undertale is a pretty cool game." "Okay yeah I like Undertale too," RetroSpecter wrote in a Reddit thread recounting their discovery, "but wtf is going on?" Crashphalt owed its unexpected renaissance, they soon realized, to Undertale Together , a fan-made Undertale multiplayer mod that, typically, only supports local co-op—a limitation that players found a clever way to circumvent. title: Cyan releases teaser for the first new Myst game in 20 years, then breaks the news that it's not actually being made
summary: Project Anglerfish looks great, but publishers apparently aren't interested.
body: Myst was a massive success: Not only was it the best-selling PC videogame of all time for years, it helped usher in the CD-ROM era, opening the door to expansive new technologies and previously unseen levels of fidelity in gaming. In 1993, Myst was nothing short of a revelation. The fortunes of Myst, and developer Cyan Worlds, have waned since then. The most recent game in the series, Myst 5: End of Ages, came out in 2005 and was reasonably well received but not a big seller; Cyan, after years of financial struggles, has moved onto Myst-like games including Firmament and Obduction, both of them reliant on crowdfunding. The studio laid off "roughly half" its staff in 2025, leading PC Gamer's Justin Wagner to write that "it's galling to see a historic indie like Cyan Worlds hit so hard" by the brutal, ongoing contraction of the game industry. Justin sure wasn't wrong about that, but some folks are finding this even more galling: Over the weekend Cyan released a teaser for a new Myst game, codenamed Project Anglerfish, which looks really good—and then said it's not in development because apparently publishers aren't interested. title: This cat-themed PC case has the best power button I've ever seen
summary: Simply the cat's pyjamas.
body: I've been watching Colorfire's cat-themed Meow product line with much interest over the years. While I've already got a kitty-eared headset , I'm sure a full feline-themed set-up would help me achieve my final form as a hardware writer. The Meow series' ME26A PC case may prove the perfect canvas towards realising that dream. In terms of styling, the ME26A is low-key compared to other entries in the Meow series. For starters, pizza-eating mascot Bobi is seemingly nowhere to be seen (unlike the Meow-X gaming PC set Colorfire showed off at last year's Computex ). There's a very fun 'Meow'-shaped air grate on the front, and even a bit of tasteful wooden trim. The cat hasn't completely left the build, though. The ME26A PC case also enjoys an almost subtle kitty paw motif, with orange decals on the chassis itself, just above the front I/O panel. Daubed in kitty pawprints, the front I/O features 1x USB-A, plus 1x USB-C port rated for up to 20 Gbps. It also happens to feature one of the best power buttons I've ever seen—if I can start my day by squishing fake toe beans, I know it's going to be a good day (via VideoCardz ). Honestly, I already can't imagine a better thing to play Cat Mail …

title: Framework 13 Pro review
summary: The best laptop Framework's ever produced, and one of the best I've ever used.
body: The moment you touch the new Framework 13 Pro laptop you know it's different to what's come before. Despite the bubblegum pink USB Type-C ports I've jammed in either side of the machine, this is a serious laptop for serious work. But it's also still instantly recognisable as one of the company's eminently upgradeable and repairable notebooks. This is the true beauty of Framework's new machine, a laptop that at once exists as the pinnacle of its hardware journey, but also steadfastly refuses to compromise on the core principles that has made it one of my favourite PC builders. Though, it must be said, that refusal to compromise here comes at a hell of a cost because of the focus on ultra expensive LPCAMM2 memory. This is a next-generation Framework laptop, but is still completely compatible with every Framework 13 device the company has shipped in the past five years or so. That is a hell of an achievement, meaning that you could have an ageing 13-inch laptop and pick and choose from the company's Marketplace store whichever parts of the new machine you wanted. If all you wanted was the beautiful new CNC aluminium chassis and input cover, go for it; if you just wanted the new touch…

title: The Pokémon Company is turning to facial recognition scans to help combat scalpers
summary: A high price to pay for your chase card.
body: Nintendo has announced the rollout of a facial recognition system and new entry and purchase rules for its Pokémon stores in Japan. It's not exactly a last-ditch effort, but it's yet another attempt at combating scalpers which have been plaguing the hobby ever since its inception. "In order to provide a safe and secure shopping environment for all customers, to prevent crime, and to ensure compliance with appropriate entry and purchase rules, we will be using a facial recognition system to verify the identity of customers," The Pokémon Company has explained in new guidance (via IGN ). The only exception to this will be Children under elementary school age, so preschoolers, up to six years old. title: PowerA LucidSound LS500/P review
summary: A potential slam dunk for budget headsets.
body: When most people are looking for a gaming headset they want it to have a few things: work with their platform of choice, sound good, decent mic, and a reasonable battery life. Other features like noise cancelling are nice but unnecessary, as well as adding to the price of the unit. The LucidSound LS500 does away with such frivolities and focuses in on what you really need in a headset, delivering a surprisingly good pair of cans for under $70 USD. Taking the headset out of the box the first thing I noticed is how light it is. The LucidSound LS500 boasts long haul battery life of up to 70 hours, so I was expecting a heavier fit. Instead it is a lightweight and comfortable headset. This is thanks to the plastic construction, which feels a little cheap but makes up for it in featherweight comfort. It even includes glasses slots to make long wear for four-eyed folks like me. It’s not as comfortable as Turtle Beach’s solution but does a far better job than the likes of top dog Razer BlackShark’s for glasses comfort. summary: Correct—you cannot improve on Leon Kennedy.
body: I am actually really excited for Zach Cregger's upcoming Resident Evil film . I think this may be the best chance there is for getting an actually good adaptation, mostly thanks to the fact that Cregger seems like a super fan who actually understands what makes the games so charming. In other words: he knows ball . "I want fans of the games to just know that I am a giant fan of the games, I am making this movie to celebrate the games—I haven't seen the other movies," Cregger said during an interview with ScreenRant . "What I'm not doing in this is that I'm not going to cannibalise the characters and the stories that the games already do so well, because I'm not going to be able to improve on Leon. summary: Load up on guns, bring your friends.
body: The era when it seemed like every second game was about zombies and the one where I played a lot of Flash games because they were free had a lot of overlap. Which is why I have fond memories of the hours I lost playing games like The Last Stand and Rebuild 2. I've just had a flashback to that time thanks to Yet Another Zombie Defense HD, which has had its price temporarily dropped by 100%. It's a twin-stick shooter where you spend the nights shooting zombies and the days building defenses, erecting barricades and saving up to buy a turret and then realizing you also need to buy a gun to mount on top of that turret. There's local and online multiplayer, a bunch of weapons and traps to unlock and modes to play, and it sure does have the look and feel of an indie game from a bygone age—even if it was only released in 2017. It's got a Steam Workshop too , where you can download skins to make your survivor look like Hatsune Miku, Garfield, Deadpool, or Shrek. Never change, Steam Workshop. title: One of the best shooters around just got a barely recognizable second episode, and it's only $12
summary: I love checking in on a New Blood game and seeing it completely transform in early access.
body: New Blood's comic book golden age noir detective immersive sim shooter, Fallen Aces, just got a beefy new update: Its second episode, Shadow of Death , is playable right now, while the usually $15 game is on sale for $12 until August 8. I'm kind of allergic to playing games in early access, so I haven't touched Fallen Aces since I fell in love with its first few levels back in 2024. Those levels were fun, the stealth tense, the combat beautifully slapstick, and the pulpy story engaging. But I mean it as a compliment when I say that the Episode 2 trailer shows a practically unrecognizable game. It's got car chases, sprawling city environments, medieval broadswords, and I lost track of how many new guns. Shout out to the cartoony Mateba Model 6 Unica in there, a.k.a the cyberpunk detective gun. The more games that sport this beautiful Italian oddity, the better. New Blood's entire main lineup of the 2020s has been slow to cook, but the three games have justified that time with ambitious increases of scope. title: Capcom wants to release a Resident Evil every year and sees remakes as the way to make it happen
summary: It's worked well so far.
body: As part of an interview in the latest issue of GameInformer (spotted via GamesRadar ), Capcom producer Masachika Kawata outlined the resurgent Japanese publisher's approach to Resident Evil: Quality and quantity, with remakes bolstering the process and helping fund the development of more adventurous projects. According to Kawata, Capcom would like Resident Evil to be a fully annual franchise, but "producing a new entry in the Resident Evil series every year would be quite an undertaking and a difficult task." That's where the remakes come in. "Being able to revisit older games and remake them helps Capcom meet that goal of releasing a Resident Evil title each year, but it also allows the team to continually challenge themselves and hone their craft," said Kawata. "That's not to say the remakes are any less important. In fact, they're just as important as the mainline titles. "Capcom is lucky enough to have found this cycle that can continue to provide us with the financial resources to create things like new entries in the Resident Evil series and completely new IP like Pragmata. So there is that relationship there." Phrases like "every year" tend to get my dander up when it come…

title: The new 'backward compatible' Xbox games on PC run on an OG Xbox emulator inside an Xbox 360 emulator, and people have already used it to run other Xbox 360 games
summary: Emulator turducken.
body: First reported by Tom's Hardware , it's come to light that, not only are the four " Backward Compatibility on PC " original Xbox games released last week running on a double layer of Xbox console emulation, but savvy independent developers have already used those emulators to run other Xbox games on PC. Developer Nathan on X, "The Everything App," has a succinct topline explanation: "The new OG Xbox Backwards Compatibility layer released by Microsoft for the PC is actually an Xbox 360 emulator running XeFu (the OG Xbox emu for the 360)," he wrote, pointing to telltale indicators visible in a dump of XeFu (the Xeon Fusion Emulator) pulled from the Fuzion Frenzy PC re-release. By combining Microsoft's recently-released PC port of XeO3 with specific components of XWine1, SlimEra namely, it becomes possible to run dumped backwards-compatible Xbox 360 and Xbox Original games before they see an official PC release, with varying degrees of success pic.twitter.com/6eocCCT1cW July 23, 2026 For an even more in-depth explanation, developer Milenko has an article on the subject, also on X. title: Red Faction: Guerrilla Re-Mars-tered review (2018)
summary: Red Faction still has the best destruction in games ever.
body: From the archives: This story originally ran in PC Gamer #321 (UK, Sep. 2018). The review appears as originally written, with only minor changes in formatting and presentation. It’s a damn crime that no game ripped off Red Faction: Guerrilla’s Geo-mod destruction feature. You take a hammer and you use it to smash out a panel of a wall and break through a pillar. Smash out a few more walls and maybe the building creaks. A few more whacks of the hammer later and the whole thing comes down, perhaps with you inside. And hey, maybe it knocks through another building on the way down. It’s still amazing to watch. Guerrilla does this one thing really well. It’s an otherwise uninspired open world game, with okay driving, unimpressive shooting and a boring story. Hell, Mars doesn’t even look that nice, because it’s Mars. But knocking down buildings in an open world is more than enough to carry this game. You’ll crash a jeep through a base. You’ll detonate mines and blow up a bridge, which will then collapse on top of an enemy settlement. You’ll melt the beams of a tower and watch it fall over.
